final_answer:
Using the cervical spinal cord bulk RNA-seq count matrix and sample metadata, I performed a covariate-adjusted differential expression analysis comparing ALS patients with controls. After sample alignment, 174 samples remained (138 ALS and 36 controls). I filtered low-count genes, then fit a DESeq2 model with design ~ rin + age_rounded + sex + library_prep + condition, where condition tested ALS versus Control and the other terms adjusted for RNA quality, demographic, and technical effects.

At adjusted p < 0.05 and |log2 fold change| >= 1, there were 404 differentially expressed genes: 213 up-regulated in ALS and 191 down-regulated in ALS.

The strongest up-regulated genes in ALS included GPNMB, CHIT1, ASAH1, PLA2G7, LYZ, DNASE2B, CTSS, HGF, IQGAP2, MS4A7, APOC1, ACP5, APOE, PPARG, and TNFSF8. These genes point to a strong glial / innate-immune / lysosomal activation signature in ALS cervical spinal cord.

Representative down-regulated genes included LINC01310, CXCL11, GACAT3, LINC00940, CACNA1B, AC093330.2, GAPDHP71, SEPHS1P6, AC073957.3, KCNG4, CERCAM, NOTCH4, OXCT2P1, VWA5B2, and AC093503.3. Among the protein-coding genes, CACNA1B and KCNG4 are notable neuron-related genes with reduced expression in ALS.

Overall, the DE genes indicate that ALS cervical spinal cord is characterized by increased inflammatory/glial transcriptional programs together with reduced expression of some neuronal-function genes. The full ranked DE table is saved in outputs/als_cervical/deseq2_results_full.tsv.
